nodes.label: EU AI Act Research Exemptions: Development-Phase and Scientific-Use
nodes.author: Janos Meszaros, Isabelle Huys, John P. A. Ioannidis
nodes.rationale: Legal analysis of EU AI Act research exemptions, arguing that distinctions between research/commercial activities and lab-based/real-world testing are increasingly blurred in contemporary AI research. Identifies regulatory grey zones and potential circumvention methods; calls for clearer guidance and stronger safeguards.

nodes.label: Development-Phase Exemption
nodes.rationale: Exempts AI systems under development before market placement or service deployment. Key limitation: testing in real-world conditions not covered by exemption. Ambiguity: 'real-world conditions' undefined; silent-mode deployment in hospital (capturing data without generating outputs) may or may not qualify depending on intended purpose interpretation.

nodes.label: Scientific-Use Exemption
nodes.rationale: Exempts AI systems specifically developed and put into service for sole purpose of scientific research. Key ambiguity: 'sole purpose' difficult to prove; goals and intentions change over time. Creates room for presenting commercially-driven systems as research to avoid regulation. Four scenarios identified where exemption applicability unclear.

nodes.label: Hypothetical Circumvention Methods for AI Act Research Exemptions
nodes.rationale: Four methods identified: (1) Offshore Cloud Deployment—testing in non-EU jurisdictions; (2) Synthetic Environment with Live Overlays—simulated environment periodically updated with live data; (3) Model-Splitting—dividing multi-model AI across systems; (4) Silent On-Site Data Capture—recording and transmitting live data without showing outputs. All would likely violate AI Act if affecting EU individuals.

nodes.label: EU AI Act Research Exemptions Analysis
nodes.author: Janos Meszaros, Ioannidis, et al.
nodes.rationale: Doctrinal legal research analyzing gaps and ambiguities in EU AI Act research exemptions, particularly the distinction between scientific research and real-world deployment

nodes.label: EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation 2024/1689)
nodes.author: European Union
nodes.rationale: Primary legal source establishing research exemptions and regulatory framework for AI systems in the EU

nodes.label: Research Exemption Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: Core regulatory gap: unclear boundary between lab-based research and real-world deployment creates opportunities for regulatory arbitrage

nodes.label: Scientific Research Definition Gap
nodes.rationale: Absence of harmonized EU-wide definition of 'scientific research' creates legal uncertainty similar to GDPR and Copyright Directive

nodes.label: Public-Private Partnership Tension
nodes.rationale: Modern research ecosystems increasingly involve collaborations between academic and commercial entities, blurring the research-commercialization boundary
